author: Charlotte Foster
title: Inside Harry and Meghan's rare Montecito home as anniversary cake leaves fans baffled - NewsBreak
text:
By Charlotte Foster Angelica Cheyenne ,
23 minutes ago Meghan Markle has offered followers an unusual peek inside her Montecito residence through several videos shared on social media, as she and Prince Harry recently commemorated their eight-year wedding anniversary.
Meghan previously posted to her now-deleted Instagram stories, uploading numerous clips featuring herself and the Duke, alongside their daughter Lilibet who remained off-camera, marking the milestone with a festive cake and the distinctive present of a sculpture depicting two embracing penguins. Observant followers noticed several details visible in the background of the footage, providing insight into her everyday life in California with her husband and two young children.
Meghan posted an image of herself and Harry kissing in their kitchen as they stood with their anniversary cake, with what looks like Archie and Lilibet's packed daily routines displayed on a whiteboard behind them.

Also visible in the background is a wooden plaque reading 'Archie's chickens', positioned near a ceramic container of fresh eggs, thought to come from the chickens Harry and Meghan raise in their yard.
Archie and Lilibet appear to have created presents for their parents' anniversary this month, with two clay figures placed in the foreground beside a card addressed to 'Mama and Papa' on its envelope. In a series of clips shared on her Instagram stories, Meghan recorded Harry as he entered their kitchen carrying a cake - the same flavor as their wedding cake - decorated with four burning candles, while Harry, Meghan and their daughter Lilibet sang "Happy anniversary to Mama and Papa" to the melody of 'Happy Birthday.'
Despite the heartwarming moment, followers were puzzled when they noticed only four candles on the cake, despite the occasion marking an eight-year anniversary. Decorated with fashionable long-stem candles, the pair appeared cheerful as they extinguished them.
Yet, some turned to social media to argue the candle count made "no sense". One individual questioned: "Eight years of marriage and only four candles?", while another asked: "Four candles? Married since 2018? The math ain't mathing..."
Nevertheless, others theorized that the four candles might represent the four family members - Harry, Meghan, their son Archie and daughter Lilibet. "For the four of them? 'Mama and Papa' and the two kids? Who knows?" one individual proposed.
Meanwhile, another thought the Prince might simply have "not had enough candles", noting: "It's the thought that counts. At least they are happy."
Meghan revealed that the family enjoyed a lemon and elderflower cake, which matches the flavor of their wedding cake from 2018. And cake creator Claire Ptak of east London's Violet Cakes, who crafted the royal wedding cake, also reminisced about the couple's wedding day. Taking to social media, Claire shared a collection of behind-the-scenes photographs documenting the cake's creation, accompanied by a heartfelt message, writing: "It's not every day you get asked to 'do what you do' and design a cake for a prince and princess with the entire world watching.
"It was discussed that we might use gilt to place the cakes on and I felt it was more personal so designed the cakes to fit the gilt platters used by generations."
She went on to add: "They were displayed in front of Elton John and his piano then lanced with Harry's sword. We had been invited into Buckingham Palace to bake the cakes safely away from paparazzi gathering outside our small bakery in East London. Thank you Meghan and Harry for trusting me and my team to make your wedding cake 8 years ago today!"
